title: Employee Offboarding in Nigeria: A Complete Guide to Exit Management, Final Payroll and Compliance
summary: Employee Management Employee Offboarding in Nigeria: A Complete Guide to Exit Management, Final Payroll and Compliance Oluwakemi Adesina August 2, 2026 When an employee decides to move on, or you have to make the hard call to let someone go, the clock starts ticking immediately. You usually have a tight two-to-four-week window to handle final pay, revoke system access, manage handovers, and sort out compliance paperwork. Handling employee offboarding in Nigeria requires a smooth process. Poorly managed exits expose your company to major risks: data leaks, lost operational knowledge, frozen vendor relationships, and costly compliance penalties. This guide provides a practical framework to transform your resignation process strategy in Nigeria. We will break down how to protect your organization, stay compliant, and calculate final payouts without the usual end-of-month panic. What Is Employee Offboarding? Simply put, the employee separation process starts when someone says “I am resigning” and ends when their name is removed from your payroll. It includes managing notice periods, collecting company assets, calculating final pay, handling legal paperwork, and transferring knowledge. Every business needs a clear, repeatable process because employee exits fall into two main legal categories: Voluntary Resignations: The employee triggers the timeline by submitting a formal notice. Your primary goal here is preserving institutional knowledge and maintaining a healthy professional relationship. Involuntary Terminations: The company starts the process. This option has more legal and compliance requirements. Every step, warning letter, and payment must be carefully documented to avoid wrongful termination claims under Nigerian labor law. Not having a clear, structured employee exit process that Nigeria teams can execute effortlessly means your business can be exposed. You need an established routine to handle separations professionally before the next unexpected resignation letter arrives. 5 Steps in an Effective Employee Offboarding Process A smooth and secure exit needs a clear step-by-step process. Whether it is a mutual separation or a sudden termination, your team should follow these five main steps in order: 1. Notice Period Management: The process begins with the employment contract. Nigerian labor laws and most contracts require a notice period of one week to three months or payment instead of notice. As soon as someone resigns or is let go, confirm it in writing. Clearly agree on the last working day to avoid confusion about the timeline. 2. Exit Documentation: Do not wait until the last day to prepare paperwork. Get the exit acknowledgement letter, clearance form, and Certificate of Service ready in advance as part of your standard process. If you use an HR automation system, quickly generate and upload these templates online. 3. Asset Recovery and Access Revocation: List all company property given to the departing employee, such as laptops, phones, tokens, access cards, and digital assets. Ensure your IT team removes their access to email, databases, and internal communication tools at the end of their last working day. 4. Structured Knowledge Transfer: Ensure important information does not leave with the employee. Meet with them to list current projects, client contacts, tasks, and file locations. Have them document workflows and hand over all project materials to the next team member or supervisor. 5. Transparent Employee Communication: Good communication prevents rumors. Inform the departing employee about the exit timeline and what to expect for their final pay. At the same time, send a short, professional update to the rest of the team about how duties are being reassigned so work continues smoothly. Managing Final Payroll During Employee Exit Most mistakes during employee exits happen when the finance team rushes payroll calculations. Getting final payroll right in Nigeria requires careful attention and a clear view of all details. Base Salary (Prorated to Last Working Day) + Unused Annual Leave Encashment + Outstanding Approved Expense Reimbursements – Statutory Deductions (PAYE, PenCom, NHF) – Outstanding Employee Loans/Company Advances = Total Clean Final Payout Start by calculating the base salary up to the employee’s last working day. Then, pay out any unused annual leave based on their current gross salary. Also, include any approved business expense reimbursements in this final payment. All legal deductions still apply during the exit process. Taxes (PAYE), pension contributions, and NHF deductions must be calculated and taken from the final payment. Past NHF payments must be checked and confirmed with the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria before closing the employee’s financial records. Compliance Requirements During Employee Separation To protect your business from audits or legal issues, your management team should check these five compliance steps before an employee leaves. Archived Employee Records: Update your centralized database with the exact termination date and reason for exit. Retain the complete employee file for the full statutory duration required by national labor regulations. Up-to-Date Tax Documentation: Provide the departing individual with their historical tax cards and necessary documentation for their next employer. Ensure their final month’s PAYE tax is accurately calculated and remitted to the relevant State Internal Revenue Service (like LIRS). Pension Fund Reconciliations: Confirm all monthly pension contributions are current, verified, and processed accurately through their specific Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) under PenCom guidelines. Centralized Signed Documentation: Store fully executed physical or digital copies of the resignation/termination letter, the completed company clearance form, and the itemized final payslip inside your secure corporate archives. Labor Law Alignment: Double-check that your enforced notice windows, severance pay multipliers (if applicable), and final disbursement timelines perfectly match the Nigerian Labour Act and the active employment contract. Common Offboarding Mistakes Businesses Should Avoid Delayed Final Payroll Disbursements: If you delay or withhold someone’s final pay after their legal exit date, it does more than upset them. It can quickly lead to serious legal trouble and expensive labor disputes for your business. Missing or Incomplete Clearance Documentation: If you skip the formal employee clearance process, you will not have proof that company property was returned or that the exit was handled properly if there is a dispute or audit later. title: The Top Used SUVs With the Best Gas Mileage in 2026
summary: If you want a spacious vehicle that delivers good gas mileage, and if you're shopping on a budget, then this list of the top used SUVs with the best gas mileage is for you.
body_text: You need a vehicle with decent cargo capacity but don't want to sacrifice fuel efficiency. If that sounds familiar, you're probably in the market for an SUV that won't punish you at the gas pump — and if you're keeping an eye on your budget, the used-car market is where the best values are waiting. Below is our curated list of some of the most fuel-efficient used SUVs available right now. We've included hybrids but excluded plug-in hybrids, since those can run on electricity alone for a portion of their range, which skews the mpg figures. Electric vehicles are also off the list, as they don't use gasoline at all (though they'd easily dominate any efficiency ranking). What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different The Top Used SUVs With the Best Gas Mileage in 2026 What Is Good Gas Mileage for a Used SUV? 2017-2024 Kia Niro 2016-2018 Toyota RAV4 Hybrid 2006-2016 Toyota Highlander Hybrid 2016-2021 Mazda CX-3 2016-2024 Honda HR-V 2020-2024 Honda CR-V Hybrid 2015-2024 Lexus NX Hybrid 2006-2008 Lexus RX Hybrid 2013-2022 Buick Encore 2011-2017 Nissan Juke Honorable Mentions Tips for Getting Good Gas Mileage in Older SUVs FAQs Shopping Tools Related Topics What Is Good Gas Mileage for a Used SUV? As a general rule, smaller vehicles tend to have better fuel efficiency. Quite a few subcompact and compact SUV models achieve an EPA combined rating of 30 mpg or better. Larger, more capable, and more off-road-oriented SUVs will typically fall considerably below the 25-mpg threshold. 2017-2024 Kia Niro Hybrid The Kia Niro Hybrid features a hard-to-argue-with number: 53 mpg combined, best-in-class for the subcompact crossover segment and verified by CarGurus during a real-world 95-mile test drive across a mix of roads and speeds — no hypermiling required. That kind of efficiency on a single 11.1-gallon tank translates to a driving range of around 588 miles between fill-ups, which puts the Niro in a class almost entirely by itself for used shoppers who want to minimize trips to the pump. The fully redesigned second-generation model also brought a sharper exterior, a more spacious interior — best-in-class cabin room, cargo space, and second-row legroom versus other subcompact crossovers — and a cabin built with sustainability in mind, with vegan leather seating made from eucalyptus fibers and a headliner sourced from recycled materials. The tradeoffs are worth knowing going in. All-wheel drive isn't available in any configuration, which limits appeal for buyers in snowier climates. The six-speed dual-clutch transmission can feel jerky at low speeds, particularly when cold, though CarGurus noted it tends to settle into a more agreeable rhythm over time. Performance is modest — 139 horsepower and a 0–62 mph time of about 10.4 seconds — so this is emphatically a commuter's car rather than an enthusiast's. But for used shoppers prioritizing fuel economy above all else, the 2023 Niro Hybrid is one of the strongest value propositions on the used market, with a comprehensive standard safety suite, a well-equipped interior from the EX trim up, and the durability that Kia's lineup has consistently demonstrated over time. The CarGurus Verdict: "A combined mpg of 53 outshines not only the Sportage’s 43 mpg but also the rest of the segment. Also, the Kia Niro offers smart design that is matched with a high-quality spacious interior. The fact that reusable and sustainable materials are used is an unexpected but much-appreciated bonus. Like its fuel economy, the Niro Hybrid does plenty good without really trying." -Beverly Braga Read our Kia Niro Buying Guide Search for Kia Niro See all 2014 Jeep Cherokee $5,317 165,650 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Austin, AR 2014 Kia Cadenza $9,299 90,061 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Phoenix, AZ 2018 Honda Civic Hatchback $16,194 111,739 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Wiscasset, ME 2021 Nissan Versa $13,188 51,510 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Bennington, VT 2017 Land Rover Discovery Sport $10,399 91,687 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Boise, ID 2023 Kia Sportage Hybrid $17,756 106,609 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Rhinelander, WI 2016-2018 Toyota RAV4 Hybrid The 2016 Toyota RAV4 Hybrid made a strong case when new, and nearly a decade later it holds up as one of the smartest used buys on this list. The powertrain pairs a 2.5-liter four-cylinder with three electric motors — two up front, one at the rear — producing 194 horsepower and delivering AWD as standard equipment, without a traditional mechanical driveshaft connecting front and rear axles. The EPA rates it at 33 mpg combined, and CarGurus verified that figure in real-world driving across a mix of city and highway. What made the original pitch compelling — and still does on the used market — is that the hybrid version was actually more powerful than the non-hybrid RAV4 of the same era while also being more efficient. That combination, from a manufacturer with Toyota's reliability reputation, makes the 2016 RAV4 Hybrid an unusually easy case for used shoppers watching fuel costs. The interior is practical and comfortable if unremarkable, with reclining rear seats, competitive cargo capacity for the segment, and a cabin layout that prioritizes ease of use. The Limited trim adds leatherette upholstery and Toyota Safety Sense P — covering pre-collision sensing, pedestrian detection, lane-departure alert, and radar cruise control, which were meaningful features for 2016. Buyers should go in clear-eyed about what a 2016 model year means: no Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, an older infotainment system, and a turning radius that CarGurus found notably wide. But for a used buyer who wants proven hybrid efficiency, standard AWD, and Toyota's long-term durability track record at an accessible price point, it remains one of the more trustworthy picks on the used market. The CarGurus Verdict: "If you were already in the market for an XLE or Limited RAV4, we strongly suggest you get the hybrid version. It truly is the perfect blend of capability, efficiency, and versatility." -George Kennedy Read our Toyota RAV4 Hybrid Buying Guide Search for Toyota RAV4 Hybrid See all 2014 Jeep Cherokee $5,317 165,650 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Austin, AR 2014 Kia Cadenza $9,299 90,061 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Phoenix, AZ 2018 Honda Civic Hatchback $16,194 111,739 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Wiscasset, ME 2021 Nissan Versa $13,188 51,510 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Bennington, VT 2017 Land Rover Discovery Sport $10,399 91,687 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Boise, ID 2023 Kia Sportage Hybrid $17,756 106,609 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Rhinelander, WI 2006-2016 Toyota Highlander Hybrid The 2016 Toyota Highlander Hybrid is one of the few three-row SUVs that can genuinely claim efficiency as a selling point. The 3.5-liter V6 runs on an Atkinson combustion cycle and pairs with two electric motors — one at the front, one at the rear — for a combined 280 horsepower and standard AWD without a traditional mechanical connection between axles. The EPA rates it at 27–28 mpg combined, and CarGurus verified close to 27 mpg over 400 mostly highway miles — a figure that compares favorably against the non-hybrid Highlander AWD's 18/24 rating and is remarkable for a vehicle that seats up to eight. Toyota's hybrid expertise is evident in the execution: the transition between gas and electric power is seamless, the V6 restarts without a shudder, and the ride is quiet and composed in a way that CarGurus compared to a Lexus RX. The interior is where the Highlander Hybrid most distinguishes itself for used shoppers. Second-row captain's chairs with reclining backs, a folding center table, and optional heating make the middle row genuinely comfortable for adults, and a panoramic moonroof and ambient lighting give the cabin a near-luxury feel well above what the exterior suggests. The Limited Platinum trim added forward collision alert with auto-braking, adaptive cruise, and lane departure warning — meaningful safety features for the era. The tradeoffs are predictable for a nearly decade-old model: no Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, an infotainment system that's functional but showing its age, and a third row that's better suited to children than adults. But for used shoppers who need three rows, AWD, and genuinely good fuel economy from a proven reliable platform, the 2016 Highlander Hybrid remains a smart and increasingly affordable find. The CarGurus Verdict: "Any other hybrid SUV this size costs way, way more, so it’s not even a contest if you’re in this market. Whether the hybrid itself is worth the premium over a loaded gas-only model is entirely up to your driving habits. For a few thousand American dollars a year, that answer would be yes." -Clifford Atiyeh Read our Toyota RAV4 Hybrid Buying Guide Search for Toyota Highlander Hybrid See all 2014 Jeep Cherokee $5,317 165,650 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Austin, AR 2014 Kia Cadenza $9,299 90,061 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Phoenix, AZ 2018 Honda Civic Hatchback $16,194 111,739 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Wiscasset, ME 2021 Nissan Versa $13,188 51,510 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Bennington, VT 2017 Land Rover Discovery Sport $10,399 91,687 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Boise, ID 2023 Kia Sportage Hybrid $17,756 106,609 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Rhinelander, WI 2016-2021 Mazda CX-3 The Mazda CX-3 earns its spot on a fuel economy list with an EPA rating of 31 mpg combined in front-drive form — verified by CarGurus' reviewer, who returned 29.2 mpg on a real-world testing loop that included mountain roads — with AWD models coming in at 29 mpg combined. But the CX-3's appeal on the used market goes well beyond the numbers. CarGurus called it "the Miata of SUVs," and that framing holds up: the 148-horsepower 2.0-liter four-cylinder isn't quick on paper, but the car weighs just 2,800 pounds, the transmission is exceptionally well-matched to the engine, and Mazda's G-Vectoring Control system subtly modulates torque in corners in a way that makes the CX-3 noticeably more composed than its class suggests. The optional predictive AWD system sends up to half the engine's power rearward before the driver senses any slip — proactive rather than reactive, which is the right approach for a small vehicle in mixed conditions. The interior punches well above its class for a used buy at this price point, with suede trim on the dashboard and door panels, full leather upholstery in Grand Touring trim, and a center console redesigned for 2019 with better storage. The Mazda Connect infotainment system responds quickly and supports natural voice recognition, though the absence of Apple CarPlay and Android Auto — an inexplicable omission even in 2019 — is a real inconvenience by today's standards. The tradeoffs are significant and worth stating plainly: the rear seat is genuinely cramped for adults, cargo space is limited even with the back seats folded, and this is emphatically a car for one or two people rather than a family hauler. But for a solo commuter or urban dweller who wants great fuel economy, an unusually premium feel, and a genuinely enjoyable driving experience from a used vehicle, the CX-3 is a compelling and now very accessible find. The CarGurus Verdict: "You don’t buy a Mazda CX-3 for off-roading capability or spending sprees at the local IKEA. You buy it because it looks terrific and is a joy to pilot, putting a smile on your face whether you’re commuting, running errands, or heading out for a drive just because." -Christian Wardlaw Search for Mazda CX-3 See all 2014 Jeep Cherokee $5,317 165,650 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Austin, AR 2014 Kia Cadenza $9,299 90,061 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Phoenix, AZ 2018 Honda Civic Hatchback $16,194 111,739 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Wiscasset, ME 2021 Nissan Versa $13,188 51,510 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Bennington, VT 2017 Land Rover Discovery Sport $10,399 91,687 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Boise, ID 2023 Kia Sportage Hybrid $17,756 106,609 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Rhinelander, WI 2016-2024 Honda HR-V The Honda HR-V took a significant step forward with the 2023 model year , now sharing architecture with the Civic rather than the Fit, and the upgrade shows throughout the car. The 2.0-liter four-cylinder delivers 158 horsepower — an improvement over the outgoing model — through a CVT with a Snow mode that adjusts transmission behavior, throttle response, and the optional AWD system for reduced-traction conditions. EPA fuel economy comes in at 28 mpg combined in front-drive form and 27 with AWD, with a 14-gallon tank taking regular fuel. Honda's full Sensing suite is now standard across every trim, including adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go — a feature absent from many far more expensive SUVs — as well as automatic emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, road-departure mitigation, traffic sign recognition, and a new wide-angle single-camera system that significantly expands the field of view versus the previous generation. Where the HR-V really earns its place on a used list is the EX-L trim, which CarGurus' reviewer found felt more expensive than its class would suggest. Perforated leather seats with additional shoulder support, dual-zone climate control, a power moonroof, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, an eight-speaker audio system, and a nine-inch touchscreen with wireless charging all come together in a package that punches well above its entry-level footprint. Cargo space checks in at 24.4 cubic feet with the rear seats up and 55.1 with them folded — among the largest in class. The CVT can feel noisy at higher speeds, there's no hybrid option (a genuine gap in the lineup), and the acceleration is modest rather than eager. But for a used buyer who wants strong standard safety tech, a genuinely refined interior, and Honda's long reliability track record at a now very accessible price, the HR-V is a compelling pick. The CarGurus Verdict: "New styling plus the newly standard Honda Sensing suite of safety features put this latest HR-V back at the front of the pack it led when it debuted in 2016." -Natalie Harrington Search for Honda HR-V See all 2014 Jeep Cherokee $5,317 165,650 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Austin, AR 2014 Kia Cadenza $9,299 90,061 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Phoenix, AZ 2018 Honda Civic Hatchback $16,194 111,739 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Wiscasset, ME 2021 Nissan Versa $13,188 51,510 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Bennington, VT 2017 Land Rover Discovery Sport $10,399 91,687 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Boise, ID 2023 Kia Sportage Hybrid $17,756 106,609 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Rhinelander, WI 2020-2024 Honda CR-V Hybrid The Honda CR-V consistently ranks among the best-selling compact SUVs on the market, and the CR-V Hybrid — which made its debut for 2020 — makes a strong case for why. The fourth-generation two-motor hybrid system pairs a 2.0-liter Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder with two electric motors for a combined 204 horsepower and an EPA-estimated 38 mpg combined, all while working transparently from the driver's seat. Real-world fuel economy will vary depending on driving conditions and terrain, but the hybrid system represents a meaningful efficiency improvement over the standard gas CR-V. The cabin is genuinely sophisticated for the class, with soft-touch materials, metal mesh air vent covers, and an interior that punches above its segment. Cargo space tops out at 76.5 cubic feet with the rear seats folded — among the largest in the compact SUV class — and rear doors that open to nearly 90 degrees make loading children and car seats easier than most rivals. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard across the lineup, with wireless versions available on the upper Sport-L and Sport Touring trims. Honda Sensing is also standard on every trim, covering adaptive cruise with stop-and-go, lane-keeping assist, lane-centering, automatic emergency braking, traffic jam assist, blind-spot monitoring, and a driver attention monitor — a suite CarGurus found performed remarkably well in extended real-world testing. The CR-V Hybrid earned an IIHS Top Safety Pick+ award, reinforcing its strong passive safety credentials. It may not be the most affordable option on the used market, but the combination of class-leading cargo space, strong safety technology, Honda's long reliability track record, and a genuinely efficient hybrid powertrain make it a hard package to pass up. The CarGurus Verdict: "Overall, there is little to criticize and much to praise about the 2024 Honda CR-V Hybrid. It might not be the most exciting vehicle in its segment, but it excels at practicality, utility, comfort, and safety." -Christian Wardlaw Search for Honda CR-V Hybrid See all 2014 Jeep Cherokee $5,317 165,650 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Austin, AR 2014 Kia Cadenza $9,299 90,061 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Phoenix, AZ 2018 Honda Civic Hatchback $16,194 111,739 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Wiscasset, ME 2021 Nissan Versa $13,188 51,510 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Bennington, VT 2017 Land Rover Discovery Sport $10,399 91,687 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Boise, ID 2023 Kia Sportage Hybrid $17,756 106,609 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Rhinelander, WI 2015-2024 Lexus NX Hybrid The Lexus NX Hybrid arrived for 2015 as an accessible entry point into the brand's luxury lineup, and on the used market it represents one of the more attainable ways to combine efficiency with a premium badge. It shares its proven powertrain with the Toyota RAV4 Hybrid — a 2.5-liter Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder paired with an electric motor for 194 combined horsepower — and posts strong EPA numbers: 32 mpg combined for the front-drive version and 31 mpg for AWD models, a meaningful improvement over the non-hybrid NX's 24 mpg. Standard AWD comes on all trim levels, and the ride is comfortable and refined. The sharp-edged exterior styling holds up well, and Lexus Safety System+ 2.0 comes standard across the board, bundling forward-collision warning, automatic emergency braking, adaptive cruise, lane departure warning with steering assist, traffic sign recognition, and blind-spot monitoring. The NX earned an IIHS Top Safety Pick+ award along with a five-star overall NHTSA rating. Cargo space trails some rivals in the compact SUV class at 16.8 cubic feet with the rear seats in place, and the rear seat is better suited to smaller adults. The infotainment relies on Lexus' Remote Touch trackpad rather than a touchscreen — Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are available, but the interface takes some getting used to. Buyers who can stretch to a 2022 or newer NX Hybrid will find a significantly redesigned model with a new platform, touchscreen infotainment, and improved efficiency. For those shopping this generation, the NX 300h is best understood as a comfortable, safe, and genuinely efficient luxury daily driver at a now very accessible used price point. The CarGurus Verdict: "The NX Hybrid has no major faults, but it falls short of expectations for a luxury vehicle." -Stephen Edelstein Search for Lexus NX Hybrid See all 2014 Jeep Cherokee $5,317 165,650 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Austin, AR 2014 Kia Cadenza $9,299 90,061 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Phoenix, AZ 2018 Honda Civic Hatchback $16,194 111,739 miles Includes dealer fees Fair Deal Wiscasset, ME 2021 Nissan Versa $13,188 51,510 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Bennington, VT 2017 Land Rover Discovery Sport $10,399 91,687 miles Includes dealer fees Good Deal Boise, ID 2023 Kia Sportage Hybrid $17,756 106,609 miles Includes dealer fees Great Deal Rhinelander, WI 2006-2008 Lexus RX Hybrid The 2008 Lexus RX 400h holds a notable place in automotive history as one of the earliest luxury hybrid SUVs, arriving at a time when the idea of a full-hybrid powertrain in a midsize luxury vehicle was genuinely novel. The setup pairs a 3.3-liter V6 with two electric motors — one at the front axle and one at the rear on AWD models, with no mechanical driveshaft connecting them — for a combined 268 horsepower. The EPA rated it at 28 mpg city and 25 mpg highway, with real-world results varying considerably depending on driving conditions and climate; owner reports suggest the hybrid system is most effective in city and suburban driving, where the electric motors carry more of the load, with colder temperatures meaningfully reducing efficiency. The cabin is quiet and refined, entry and egress are easy, and the RX's signature ride comfort remains a genuine strength nearly two decades later. For used shoppers considering a vehicle this age, context matters. There is no Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, or any modern connectivity — the infotainment is a DVD-based navigation system of its era. Nickel-metal hydride hybrid battery longevity is a key variable to investigate before purchase, and buyers should factor in the cost of potential battery replacement. Cargo space behind the rear seats is tighter than the non-hybrid RX due to battery placement, and the rear seat is best suited to two adults rather than three. At this price point on the used market, the 2008 RX 400h is best suited to buyers who prioritize city fuel savings and a smooth, quiet luxury experience over modern technology — and who are diligent about pre-purchase inspection. Buick's QuietTuning noise isolation is a genuine differentiator at this segment and price point, giving the Encore a calmer, more refined cabin feel than most subcompact rivals. Cargo capacity is on the modest side — 19 cubic feet behind the rear seats and 48 with them folded flat — but the passenger seat folds flat for longer items, a useful practical touch. Used shoppers should pay close attention to how the example they're considering was optioned, as advanced safety features are not standard here. Blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, forward-collision warning, and lane-departure warning all require add-on packages that not every buyer selected — so it's worth confirming what's actually equipped before purchase. The Encore was discontinued after the 2023 model year, making well-optioned used examples the last of their kind, and the combination of Buick's refined character, accessible used pricing, and solid fuel economy makes it a sensible pick for urban or suburban buyers who prioritize comfort and efficiency over cargo space or the latest driver-assist tech. FWD and AWD configurations are both available, with the AWD system including torque-vectoring technology that meaningfully improves handling composure. Tips for Getting Good Gas Mileage in Older SUVs The Top Used SUVs With the Best Gas Mileage FAQs Which used hybrid SUV gets the best gas mileage? The Kia Niro Hybrid stands out at the top of the efficiency chart, delivering an impressive 43 to 50 mpg combined depending on the trim level. The Honda CR-V Hybrid is another strong performer, earning an EPA-estimated 38 mpg — making it one of the most fuel-efficient options in the compact SUV segment. Are there fuel-efficient used SUVs that also offer AWD? Yes, several models on this list pair solid fuel economy with standard or available AWD. The 2016-2018 Toyota RAV4 Hybrid comes standard with AWD and still achieves 32 mpg combined, while the Lexus NX Hybrid offers AWD with a 31 mpg combined rating — both strong choices if you need traction in winter weather or on unpaved roads. How can I improve the gas mileage on an older used SUV? A few simple habits can make a meaningful difference in real-world efficiency. Keep your tires inflated to the recommended pressure, avoid carrying unnecessary cargo, accelerate gently from stops, and coast gradually toward traffic lights rather than braking hard at the last moment. What Makes CarGurus Best Cars Guides Different? Most car-shopping websites publish lists of the best cars across a variety of categories, with recommendations generally driven by editorial expertise. Here's what makes ours different: In addition to the insights and verdicts of our team of car-testing experts, our best cars guides take into account other factors that we know matter to buyers-real owner experiences and current market value. title: How Cape Fox FCG combines CRM and AI agents to increase BD output
body_text: About Cape Fox FCG Cape Fox Federal Contracting Group (FCG) is a division of the Cape Fox Corporation (CFC), an Alaska Native Corporation (ANC) established for the village of Saxman under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (ANCSA). Cape Fox FCG delivers professional IT, healthcare, logistics, and construction services to U.S. federal agencies. We sat down with Tim Blaszkow, a Federal Growth Executive and AI-innovator at Cape Fox FCG, to discuss their use of GovDash across their BD lifecycle. Turning CRM and AI agents into BD leverage Cape Fox uses GovDash as its primary CRM across 12 federal subsidiaries , giving its business development team a single system to manage pipeline, organize customer intelligence, and support capture work at scale. The team has scaled to 20–25 total users , and actively manages 15–20 opportunities at a time in the GovDash platform. By combining CRM workflows with AI agents and skills, Cape Fox has reduced manual research, improved opportunity coverage, and increased output without adding team resources over the past year. The challenge Before GovDash, Cape Fox relied on an internal SharePoint-based solution to manage BD information. As the team scaled its capture and pipeline work, it needed a better way to centralize data, organize field intelligence, and reduce the time spent turning raw notes into actionable insight. The goal was straightforward: let BD and capture teams spend more time engaging customers and less time sorting through documents, tracking information manually, and assembling research. The solution Cape Fox adopted GovDash as its primary CRM and now uses it as its “source of truth for BD.” Capture managers use GovDash as part of a repeatable workflow: meet with customers and collect raw notes link those notes and materials to the opportunity record query GovDash to organize the information and surface relevant insight That workflow supports several core use cases: customer engagement tracking competitor tracking technology integration analysis Cape Fox also uses agents and skills primarily in early-stage BD and capture , as well as proposal and compliance workflows. One of their most valuable agent workflows kicks off as soon as a new opportunity enters the pipeline. The agent compiles an initial competitive landscape by gathering and organizing context such as: agency budget strategic plan information stakeholder mapping funding and reorganization signals As Cape Fox’s use of the platform evolved, the team also shifted some workflows from agents into skills when they proved to be a better fit for more irregular processes. “GovDash is our source of truth for BD.” “Each capture manager is able to take on more opportunities because they’re not having as much time tied up in sorting through data and trying to pull out insights.” Accelerating BD work GovDash has helped Cape Fox create measurable efficiency gains in its BD process. One example is its competitive analysis workflow, which saves 3–4 hours every time it runs compared with manual research. Just as importantly, the team reports increased output over the past year without adding headcount . Key metrics from the deployment include: 12 federal subsidiaries using the platform 15–20 active opportunities managed at a time Beyond CRM: new ways to work Cape Fox’s use of GovDash has expanded beyond structured CRM workflows. The team also uses the platform for: strategic planning white space analysis market prioritization It is also actively using document generation to create branded first drafts of RFI responses, helping accelerate downstream proposal work. Cape Fox also highlighted project management and deliverables extraction as an important emerging area, especially as operations teams become more consistent about contributing data upstream. GovDash as a source of truth Cape Fox described GovDash as its “source of truth for BD” and emphasized that the platform helps its capture managers focus less on manual information processing and more on customer engagement. The team also pointed to the pace of product iteration as a major positive and did not raise any immediate feature gaps during the conversation.

title: Watch Out for a Fed Pause
summary: A cooling labor market, easing inflation and record AI-related bond issuance are shaping Morgan Stanley Research's outlook for Fed policy and fixed income.
body_text: Markets are pricing in at least one more interest-rate increase from the U.S. Federal Reserve this year following hotter inflation data and a more hawkish tone from policymakers. Consumer prices rose 3.5% in the year through June, less than markets expected and a slowdown from 4.2% in May, which was the highest annual increase in three years. Meanwhile, new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has emphasized that restoring price stability is his top priority, and the median projection from Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) participants points to one rate hike in 2026. Morgan Stanley Research, however, sees a different path. “We expect a lower inflation trajectory that keeps policy on hold this year, potentially followed by two rate cuts in 2027 as inflation gradually normalizes,” says Michael Gapen, Chief U.S. Economist for Morgan Stanley Research. “The main source of this divergence is our more constructive view on the inflation outlook relative to both markets and the Fed.” For fixed-income investors, a stable-to-easing rate environment could support government bonds and reinforce the case for maintaining exposure to high-quality income-generating assets. “A broadly unchanged Fed policy-rate path in 2026 and the prospect of AI-driven productivity gains should keep real yields elevated,” says Vishy Tirupattur, Chief Fixed Income Strategist and Director of Quantitative Research at Morgan Stanley. Why the Fed May Hold Rates Steady Morgan Stanley Research expects the Fed to keep rates unchanged for several reasons. First, inflation appears to be moderating as the pass-through from higher tariffs to consumer prices is nearing completion, reducing a key source of pressure. In addition, leading indicators suggest rent and housing inflation continue to cool. Lower energy prices should also help ease inflation. After surging above $120 a barrel during the height of tensions surrounding the conflict in Iran, Brent crude futures fell below $70 in the final week of June as geopolitical risks eased. Morgan Stanley Research commodity strategists expect Brent crude to end 2027 around $70 a barrel. Recent labor market data further reinforce Morgan Stanley Research’s expectation that the Fed will leave rates unchanged this year, instead of raising them. The U.S. economy added 57,000 jobs in June, well below the consensus estimate of 115,000, while payroll gains for the previous two months were revised lower by a combined 74,000 jobs. “The data suggests labor demand is cooling after a stronger spring,” Gapen says. “Based on what we know now, we think patience will win the day and the Fed will not hike in July.” Financial Conditions Already Reflect Tighter Policy Meanwhile, financial markets have already done much of the Fed’s tightening, notes Martin Tobias, U.S. Interest Rate Strategist for Morgan Stanley Research. Tobias and his team developed a financial conditions index modeled on a framework used by the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco. The index incorporates 12 market variables—including Treasury yields, mortgage rates and corporate borrowing spreads—to estimate the effective level of monetary policy implied by financial conditions. Since the start of the Iran conflict, the index suggests financial conditions have tightened by an amount equivalent to four 25-basis-point rate increases. “In essence, markets have already priced in the persistent inflation risks identified by the FOMC by pushing the implied Fed funds rate path higher,” Tobias says. “The Fed doesn’t need to deliver on the tightening in financial conditions in response to backward-looking data to retain credibility. It just needs to react to incoming information.” Warsh has signaled that under his watch the Fed will give fewer hints about where rates are headed, which gives investors less to anchor to between central bank meetings. That means big economic releases, like inflation and jobs reports, can move expectations more and short‑term rates may swing more as markets reprice what the Fed might do next. “Less forward guidance should mean more policy surprises—and therefore greater realized volatility,” Tobias says. “We continue to see attractive medium-term value in short- and intermediate-maturity bonds,” which may be less sensitive to the volatility in short-term rates than longer-duration government bonds. Fixed Income Outlook Against a backdrop of less forward guidance and greater potential for policy surprises, Morgan Stanley Research’s views emphasize where income and relative value appear compelling. While equities remain the preferred engine of portfolio returns, fixed income has regained an important role as a source of income, diversification and stability. Elevated yields and a generally supportive economic backdrop create a constructive environment for bond investors, but record issuance across many sectors is likely to limit broad-based price appreciation. As a result, returns are expected to be driven more by income and security selection than by falling yields or significant spread tightening, reinforcing fixed income’s role as a portfolio stabilizer rather than a primary return driver. Here’s a breakdown for fixed income investors: Government bonds appear positioned for gradual improvement as inflation likely moderates and the Fed remains on hold. Morgan Stanley Research projects the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury to decline to approximately 4.25% by year-end and 4.20% in 2027, supporting a constructive—but not overly bullish—outlook for U.S. government bonds. Relative value opportunities may also emerge in parts of Europe and Japan. Investment-grade credit remains supported by resilient corporate fundamentals, but supply is likely to be the defining theme. Morgan Stanley Research forecasts a record $2.25 trillion of U.S. investment-grade issuance this year, which is expected to put modest upward pressure on spreads and limit price appreciation. As a result, returns are likely to be driven primarily by income, producing solid mid-single-digit total returns. High yield sectors continue to offer attractive income generation opportunities. Morgan Stanley Research expects high-yield bonds to generate total returns of approximately 6% to 7%, supported by a resilient economic backdrop. However, as defaults gradually rise, sector allocation and issuer selection are expected to play a greater role in determining outcomes. Structured credit and municipals may offer attractive risk-adjusted income while reinforcing fixed income’s role as a portfolio stabilizer.
